about.text: At issue is whether the Federal Election Campaign Act’s limits on coordinated campaign expenditures, which restrict political parties from spending money on campaign advertising with input from the party’s candidate for office, violate the First Amendment.

caseName: NRSC, et al v. FEC, et al

events.description: OPINION and JUDGMENT filed : IT IS THE JUDGMENT of the En Banc Court of the Sixth Circuit that the Federal Election Campaign Act’s limits on coordinated campaign expenditures do not violate the First Amendment. Mandate to issue. Decision for publication. Jeffrey S. Sutton, Chief Judge (AUTHORING); Karen Nelson Moore, Eric L. Clay, Julia Smith Gibbons, Richard Allen Griffin, Raymond M. Kethledge, Jane Branstetter Stranch (CONCURRING IN THE JUDGMENT), Amul R. Thapar (CONCURRING), John K. Bush (CONCURRING DUBITANTE), Joan L. Larsen, John B. Nalbandian, Chad A. Readler (DISSENTING), Eric E. Murphy, Stephanie Dawkins Davis, Andre B. Mathis, and Rachel Bloomekatz (CONCURRING IN THE JUDGMENT), Circuit Judges. *Pursuant to the opinion correction letter of 9/6/24 (DE 53), the opinion attached to this entry has been corrected.--[Edited 09/06/2024 by CL]
